summary: 1934 steel fire tower in the Great Smokies, built by the PWA and NPS; in poor shape in 2013, with restoration plans since 2007 and unclear results.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab

access.note: Wikipedia says the tower is accessible to the public. A January 2013 article described rusting bolts, rotting floor planks and missing guardrails. No current park notice found.

visit.trail_note: Reached by the Appalachian Trail and a short spur trail that is about 3.5 miles from the parking lot on the north side of Fontana Dam; Wikipedia calls the hike strenuous.

events.note: Register: built by the Public Works Administration and the National Park Service
Registered March 19, 2007; nominated by Peter Barr
Group hike to visit the tower and evaluate its condition; chapter report says over $700 was raised for restoration
Severe vandalism over the past year, as reported in a January 2013 article
Article describes rusting bolts, rotting floor planks, broken windowpanes and missing guardrails; about $4,000 held for repairs
Chapter report lists the tower as rehabilitated; its 2016 goals still planned an announcement for the restoration

notes_for_editor: No source after 2016 gives the tower's condition or access; the Wikipedia access line is undated. The 2015 report says rehabilitated while the 2016 goals still plan a restoration announcement, so the story says the record is unclear. Staffing history (NPS staffing until the late 1960s, cabin removed 1987) appeared only in search snippets, so it is left out. The record's height_m stays null: the register's 60 ft is the tower height, and the cab-floor height is not sourced. Quotes from the 2013 article come from an archived copy with no named publisher.
